review_result: Boot EIINT entry: SYNCP then branch to context-save body 10C. Executed through real state1 timer callback and EIRET; no normal C arguments or return contract. FPEC=0 and manually seeded architectural interrupt context; not physical interrupt acquisition or timing.

Save r6/EIPC/EIPSW; read EIIC into r6; EI; save r1..lp; call 748; restore GPRs; DI; restore EIPSW/EIPC/r6; EIRET. Full execution preserves all 31 GPRs and stack canaries; restores PSW and clears ISPR. Pending-FPI and nested-interrupt behavior are not exercised.

Walk eight-byte EIIC/handler records from TP=869C until exact cause or FFFFFFFF sentinel; call selected handler. Eight records include the default. Cause27F selects default1EA4 despite a following 27F/32A0 pair; that pair is not part of this traversal. Boot timer1087 executes through 1E44. No physical interrupt routing experiment.

Boot callback for EIIC1087: TAUJ0 channel2 per P1M-E R01UH0585EJ0120 page284. Calls1CE8 ->1E04 ->14A2; state byteFEBF2904==2 enters services while state1 returns. Exact state1 chain and interrupt return executed without callee replacement; state2 services and physical scheduling are not exercised.

Boot phase: copies exactly 0xCB words from CodeFlash 0x8370..0x869B to RAM 0xFEBF1000..0xFEBF132B, reads back the last word, SYNCM/SYNCI. Full copied span and both canaries executed. RAM callback FEBF12B8 maps to ROM 8628 only in this phase; application crypto reuses the RAM. Physical cache timing is not established.

Forward byte-counted copy: r6 destination, r7 source, r8 byte count; returns original destination in r10. Word path requires both pointers four-byte aligned; otherwise byte path. Exact firmware execution covers aligned bulk/tail and unaligned copies, unchanged source, destination canaries and stack restoration. Not an overlap-safe memmove contract.

Byte-counted zero fill: r6 destination, r7 byte count, no return contract. Short unaligned and 128-byte-block-plus-tail paths execute with exact destination and canary checks. Uses byte alignment prelude, 128/64/32/16-byte blocks and word/byte tails; zero count makes no destination write in the separate exhaustive boundary smoke.

Encode 4-bit or 46-bit freshness into one or six MSB-first bytes. Capacity admission compares only the low byte of the uint32 in/out capacity. Insufficient capacity preserves output and capacity; otherwise unsupported format sets capacity zero without writing output. Supported output reports bit length and zeroes unused trailing wire bits. Exact execution checks both formats, low-byte capacity rejection, unsupported format, source preservation and canaries.

Decode exact bit lengths 4 and 46 into a 12-byte wire record: trip32 +0, reset32 +4, message16 +8, reset-low2 +10, bit length +11. Truncated format reads one byte and zeroes trip/reset; full format reads six bytes containing 16/20/8/2 bits. Unsupported full-word lengths zero the entire record without reading input. Execution checks unused wire bits, unaligned source, exact initialized source extent, canaries and an unmapped unsupported-format source. This decoder's zero marker is not a complete transaction rejection.

Ordered reset search reloads FEBE55C4 each attempt and considers current,-1,+1,-2,+2 within 0..0xFFFFF. Match low bits and skip the requested unsigned16 matching ordinal; return 1 with candidate/index or 0 when exhausted. Failed candidate value is unspecified. Exact execution checks ambiguous -2/+2 selection and both counter boundaries. Raw 909CA..90A47 preserves r6-r9; sole caller 90B76 forwards them at 90B7E. Inline real p-code to retain that actual register dataflow rather than imposing generic caller-saved kills.

Read current trip and selected committed history; newer trip/reset seeds message from received low bits. Same epoch rebuilds message congruence and optionally advances one interval. Reset ceiling or message overflow yields message FF with return 0; the outer wrapper interprets the sentinel. Older epoch returns 0x23 while candidate index <4, otherwise 0x22, without output writes. Successful output writes ten bytes and preserves the opaque tail. Executed new-epoch low2 values 0..3, wrap, saturation, stale epochs and width8 behavior; retained fixtures protect distinct boundaries.

Compose ordered reset search and message reconstruction using explicit output pointer r9. Message width is clamp(bit_length-2,0,8); reset-low width is two except input bit lengths 0 or1 are retained. Matching ordinal can move an older -2 candidate returning 0x23 to an admissible +2 candidate. No candidate returns 0x22 without output writes. A zeroed unsupported-format parse record is not independently rejected here: the executed new-epoch case reconstructs message0. This is a direct helper boundary, not proof of CAN or authenticated-transaction admission.

For unsigned slot <2 and low-byte result ==1, copy 12 bytes from pending FEBE55F4+12*slot to committed FEBE55DC+12*slot inside the ordinary critical section. Executed second-slot commit, invalid slot rejection, nonboolean result rejection and low-byte truncation; pending source and nesting count preserved. Not rollback and not PDU dequeue.

Sixteen signed-x/unsigned-y points in a 0x44-byte row; last four bytes not read. Upper clamp uses point15; lower inputs extrapolate segment0. Interpolated value narrows to unsigned16 with signed16 denominator. Signed16 second output blends maxima of neighboring quantized slopes and rescales Q8 to Q9 without saturation; duplicate-x slope fallback comes from AF88C. 54 exact-image executions cover real-row knots and boundaries plus duplicate-x fallbacks. Physical units and all malformed-table/native arithmetic exceptional cases remain outside the executed boundary.
